title: [Switch 2, Preorder] Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity - Definitive Edition $47.45 (50% off) for Existing Owners @ Nintendo eShop
body:
Deal: [Switch 2, Preorder] Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity - Definitive Edition $47.45 (50% off) for Existing Owners @ Nintendo eShop

[belongsinforums] 50% off if you already own it is a deal? Isn't this normal price? When does the deal expire?
[ShadowStealer7] 50% off if you already own it is a deal?
It's admittedly a rubbish title, but that's the best I can get with the character limit.
When does the deal expire?
No expiry
[TheDukeOfNukem] So it's not really a deal then, more of a permanent always available offer.
[bargainatoraah] Makes me think of all the other Nintendo titles I own twice
[Ryballs] It's sad that rebuying games you already own has become the new normal.
[ShadowStealer7] Especially considering how poor this game runs on Switch 1, it's baffling that it's not a free upgrade or even a cheaper "upgrade pack" DLC like Nintendo usually do. The only caveat here is that if you don't already own the DLC it makes it a slightly better deal, if you do unfortunately there's no extra discount…
[Valkian24] That's how companies Koei Tecmo and Square Enix do it cause they don't care about being kind to their consumers.
[deeeno] If you borrow a Switch 1 copy from the library/friend, then access the 50% off, is it yours to keep digitally without the original catridge?
[Edwardrw] Yes I am curious about it as I can rent it from one of the local libraries around my house.
[ShadowStealer7] I would assume so? I know that works for Hogwarts Legacy, which is in the same sort of situation as this where it is a discounted version of the full game as the "upgrade".
It would make it a historic low price for a digital version of either the Switch 1 or Switch 2 releases if it does work like that, since that has never gone below $53 without any DLC, and it hasn't been discounted on the eShop for over a year now.
[YoursTruly] Absurd
Game isn’t anything special to write home about to demand such a price - for existing owners. (Should be a free upgrade or $10 max)
Nintendo is milking anything Zelda like it’s Lon Lon milk
[789] Good to know, but this really does nothing to improve my perception of Nintendo. They really should take a leaf out of CD Projekt Red's book
[pj1351] I definitely think the "deal" sucks, but your perception regarding this shouldn't really be directed to Nintendo.
A wide variety of Nintendo's games have low-price or free upgrades to the Switch 2 editions, and so far all Nintendo 1st/2nd party Switch 2 titles with "physical" release to-date has been full game on cart.
The sole exception has been Pokemon Pokopia as a GKC release, which is published by Koei Tecmo in Japan (basically calling the shots as the main publisher).
Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity Definitive Edition will be the second GKC exception. And if you have a look at who the main publisher of the game is, you might see a familiar name.
Not exactly the same situation per-se, but it would be a lot like having a certain perception towards Sega regarding Bayonetta 2 and 3, when Nintendo is the main publisher for those two games.
[justtoreply] Imprisonment was an interesting start but quickly degenerated into nothing more than beat 3 enemies to pass the level. It massively outstayed its welcome with inane side quests. I cant imagine willingly buying another warriors game
[pj1351] $10 or even $20 as an upgrade pack with additional contents would be acceptable.
But needing to effectively buy the game again? I'll stick to playing the Switch 1 version on the Switch 2.
